Jason.what: Chosen leader of the Argonauts, Jason comforts Alcimede and launches the Argo.
Jason kills King Cyzicus by mistake in the night battle and reconciles with Telamon.
Jason proposes words before force and leads a party to Aeetes' palace.
Jason meets Medea at Hecate's shrine and receives the Prometheus charm.
Jason yokes the fire-breathing bulls, sows the teeth and defeats the earthborn warriors with a boulder.
Jason ambushes and kills Apsyrtus, then is purified by Circe.

Medea.what: Eros's arrow wounds Medea, who is consumed by love for Jason.
Medea promises Chalciope help, nearly poisons herself, then gives Jason the charm.
Medea flees her home, lulls the serpent and helps Jason seize the fleece.
Medea reproaches Jason and lures her brother Apsyrtus into the ambush.
Medea begs Arete and the heroes at Drepane for protection.
Medea bewitches the bronze giant Talos, who wounds his ankle and falls.

Hera.what: Hera and Athena persuade Cypris to make Medea love Jason.
Hera turns Medea from suicide and makes Jason splendid.
Hera drives Medea to flee and sends a wind carrying the Argo.
Hera drives the ship back with storms after the murder.
Hera sends Iris to Thetis and watches the Argo through the Wandering rocks.

Heracles.what: Heracles refuses leadership of the Argonauts.
Heracles rebukes the crew for lingering at Lemnos.
Heracles breaks his oar, loses Hylas and is left behind.
The Hesperides tell how Heracles struck water from a rock.

Orpheus.what: Orpheus stops the quarrel of Idas and Idmon with a song of creation.
Orpheus directs the rites at Electra's island and Dindymum.
Orpheus' lyre overpowers the Sirens' song.
Orpheus sings at the wedding of Jason and Medea.
Orpheus advises offering the tripod to Triton.

Peleus.what: Peleus rallies the despairing crew after Tiphys dies.
Thetis tells Peleus to sail at dawn.
Peleus interprets the golden-maned sea-horse as a guide.

Aeetes.what: Aeetes sets Jason the trial of the bulls and the teeth.
Aeetes hands over the teeth and watches Jason win, returning grieving.
Aeetes pursues the fleeing Argo with the Colchians.

Argus.what: Argus tells the Argonauts the story of Phrixus's sons and warns of Aeetes.
Argus explains the Argonauts' errand to Aeetes at the banquet.
Argus advises the new route by the Ister.

Apollo.what: The poet invokes Apollo and Jason sacrifices to him.
Apollo appears at dawn on Thynias to the Argonauts.
Apollo reveals the island Anaphe and saves the Argonauts from darkness.

Idas.what: Idas boasts that nothing will defeat the Argonauts.
Idas mocks the gods and quarrels with Idmon.
Idas kills the boar that slew Idmon.
Idas scoffs at seeking Medea's help.

Athena.what: Athena pushes the Argo through the Clashing Rocks.
Athena and Hera plan how Jason can win the fleece.

Chalciope.what: Chalciope greets her sons and laments in Aeetes' palace.
Chalciope begs Medea to save her sons and Medea promises.
Chalciope questions Medea in vain about what she has done.

Mopsus.what: Mopsus interprets the halcyon's cry, leading to sacrifice to Rhea.
Mopsus dies of a serpent's bite in Libya.

Polydeuces.what: Polydeuces kills King Amycus in a boxing match.
Polydeuces helps Jason yoke the bulls.

Tiphys.what: Tiphys rouses the crew and steers the Argo from Pagasae.
Tiphys rejoices as the Argo escapes the Clashing Rocks.

Apsyrtus.what: Apsyrtus leads the Colchian fleet and cuts across to block the Argo.
Apsyrtus is lured by Medea and killed by Jason.

Cypris.what: Cypris agrees reluctantly and bribes Eros to strike Medea.
Cypris saves Butes after he leaps overboard to the Sirens.

Castor.what: Castor helps Polydeuces against Amycus and the Bebrycians.
Castor helps Jason yoke the bulls.

Hecate.what: Hecate Brimo appears to Jason with serpents, torches and hounds.

Phineus.what: Phineus, tormented by Harpies, is freed and prophesies the route to Colchis.
Phineus tells of Paraebius's inherited curse.

Telamon.what: Telamon angrily blames Jason for leaving Heracles, then is reconciled.
Telamon goes with Aethalides to ask Aeetes for the seed.

Ancaeus.what: Hera inspires Ancaeus, who takes the helm after Tiphys dies.
Ancaeus despairs as the Argo is stranded in the Syrtis.

Calais.what: Calais and Zetes chase the Harpies from Phineus.

Cheiron.what: Chiron bids the Argonauts farewell from the shore.

Euphemus.what: Euphemus releases the dove before the Clashing Rocks.
Euphemus receives Triton's clod, which becomes the island Thera.

Pelias.what: Pelias, warned by an oracle, devises the quest for Jason.

Zetes.what: Zetes and Calais chase the Harpies and are stopped by Iris.

Circe.what: Circe, shaken by dreams, purifies Jason and Medea.
Circe questions Medea, sees through her and sends them away.

Hypsipyle.what: Hypsipyle receives the Argonauts and offers Jason the kingship.

Idmon.what: Idmon prophesies return for most but death for himself.
A boar kills Idmon, and the heroes bury him.

Prometheus.what: The Argonauts see Prometheus bound with his eagle.

Aethalides.what: Aethalides persuades Hypsipyle to receive the Argonauts.

Alcinous.what: Alcinous rules Medea stays with Jason if already wed.

Arete.what: Arete pleads for Medea and secretly sends word to Jason to marry.

Argo.what: The Argo's oak beam speaks, telling them to seek Circe.

Canthus.what: Canthus is killed by Caphaurus in Libya.

Hylas.what: Hylas is drawn into the spring by a nymph.

Iris.what: Iris stops the Boreads from killing the Harpies.
Iris carries Hera's message to Thetis, Hephaestus and Aeolus.

Lycus.what: Lycus welcomes the Argonauts and offers his son Dascylus as guide.

Phrontis.what: Phrontis and his brothers are shipwrecked, meet Jason and learn they are kin
Medea calls to Phrontis at the river, and he helps her board the Argo

Polyphemus.what: Polyphemus hears Hylas' cry and tells Heracles, then is left behind

Thoas.what: Thoas, spared by his daughter, is the only man of Lemnos left alive

Sthenelus.what: Sthenelus' ghost appears at his tomb as the Argonauts halt

Aegle.what: Aegle, turned into a willow, tells the Argonauts how Heracles struck water from rock

Alcimede.what: Alcimede weeps and clings to Jason, who comforts her before he leaves

Amphidamas.what: Amphidamas advises scaring the birds of Ares with noise and a roof of shields

Amycus.what: Amycus forces strangers to box and is killed by Polydeuces with a blow

Aretus.what: Aretus aids Amycus, and the Bebrycians are routed by the heroes

Autolycus.what: Autolycus and his brothers join the Argonauts at Sinope

Butes.what: Butes leaps overboard lured by the Sirens and is saved by Cypris

Cleite.what: Cleite, Cyzicus' bride, hangs herself after his death

Cyrene.what: Cyrene, loved by Apollo, bears Aristaeus, who ends a plague on Ceos

Cytissorus.what: Cytissorus and his brothers are shipwrecked and meet Jason, their kin

Cyzicus.what: Cyzicus hosts the Argonauts, then is killed by Jason in the night battle

Dascylus.what: Lycus offers his son Dascylus to the Argonauts as guide

Deileon.what: Deileon and his brothers join the Argonauts at Sinope

Eretheis.what: Eretheis, turned into an elm, tells how Heracles made water gush

Erginus.what: Erginus eagerly offers to steer after Tiphys dies

Eros.what: Eros is bribed by Cypris with a golden ball and flies down to earth
Eros unseen shoots Medea, who is consumed by love for Jason

Ganymedes.what: Ganymedes plays dice with Eros when Cypris finds them

Glaucus.what: Glaucus rises from the sea and reveals the fates, reconciling Jason and Telamon

Harpies.what: The Harpies swoop down and snatch Phineus' food, until the sons of Boreas drive them off.

Heliades.what: The Heliades, turned to poplars, weep amber for Phaethon beside the Eridanus.

Hesperus.what: Hesperus, turned into a poplar, tells of Heracles, who made water gush from the rock.

Iphinoe.what: Iphinoe invites the Argonauts to the city and brings them to Hypsipyle.

Nauplius.what: Nauplius is eager to steer, but the crew choose Ancaeus as helmsman.

Nereids.what: The Nereids toss the Argo between the Wandering rocks and guide it safely.

Oileus.what: Oileus is wounded by a feather from the birds of Ares.

Paraebius.what: Paraebius, Phineus' friend, suffers his father's inherited curse and is freed by the heroes.

Polyxo.what: Polyxo urges the Lemnian women to take the strangers as protectors and husbands.

Sirens.what: The Sirens sing, but Orpheus' lyre overpowers them and Butes is saved by Cypris.

Talos.what: Talos blocks the landing on Crete, is bewitched by Medea, wounds his ankle and falls.

Thetis.what: Thetis agrees to Hera's request, gathers the Nereids and tells Peleus to sail at dawn.
